summary: Independent auditor that tests your AI agent in a simulation of your business to catch risky actions and blind spots before launch.

heroCommands.comment: Try the demo audit (no API key)
heroCommands.command:
pip install ifixai
ifixai author reference -o reference.yaml
ifixai validate reference.yaml
ifixai run --provider mock --eval-mode self --fixture reference.yaml

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: iFixAi audits AI agents before you trust them with real work. It places your agent in a simulation of your business, sends it the kinds of requests a real day brings, including risky ones, and grades how it behaves against your goals, rules and who may do what.
sixtySeconds.problem: It's hard to know whether an agent will respect your business rules or do something it shouldn't. iFixAi combines red teaming, governance and assurance checks into a repeatable audit you can run yourself or from your coding agent.
whoFor: Teams shipping AI agents to production
Developers testing support or ops agents
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for an independent, repeatable agent audit that shows the cost before running and works from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other tools.
requirements: An API key for the judge model (not needed for the demo)
Your agent's endpoint and token for real audits

overview: The quick start runs a demo with a built-in mock agent and canned grades, so you see the flow without any API key. It builds a simulation for a fictional fintech support agent and runs the 10 default inspections.

The recommended way is from your coding agent: install the plugin (Claude Code, Codex) or the skill (Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Zed and more) and ask it to run iFixAi on your agent. It builds the environment and shows the cost before anything is billed.
There is also a guided CLI: describe your agent in a profile, build and validate its environment, set up the run with ifixai setup, then run with --dry-run first. The project is Apache-2.0 licensed.

tutorial.title: Audit your own agent
tutorial.useCase: Describe your agent, build its simulation and do a dry run first.

steps.title: Describe your agent
steps.body: Copy the reference profile to my-agent.json and edit it.

steps.title: Build and check the environment
steps.code:
ifixai author my-agent.json -o my-agent.yaml
ifixai validate my-agent.yaml

steps.title: Set up and dry-run
steps.code:
ifixai setup
export AGENT_API_KEY=...
ifixai run --fixture ./my-agent.yaml --api-key "$AGENT_API_KEY" --dry-run

tutorial.expected: A graded report of how your agent handled the simulated requests.
